=== BEGIN ARTIFACT TOPOLOGY.md === ## Declarations ## story foundation summary: Stand up the Python project tree, the mdparser package skeleton, and the pytest runner. type: foundational kind: capability phase: 1 implements: ARCHITECTURE.md stack: common.md, python.md provides: mdparser package, pytest test runner acceptance: yes instructions: | Create the language foundation at the project root: pyproject.toml, a committed uv.lock, a .venv created by uv venv, launchers under bin/, and a tests/ directory with a conftest.py. Use only the Python standard library at runtime. Create an empty importable package named mdparser. Do not name it commonmark, so it cannot be mistaken for a public Markdown library. Reserve these modules with documented responsibilities and no behavior yet: blocks, inlines, refs, entities, render, and cli. ARCHITECTURE.md records the two-phase design from the spec Appendix: phase 1 builds the block tree and collects link reference definitions, and phase 2 parses inlines with the delimiter stack. It also records these decisions: - Entities come from the Python standard library table html.entities.html5. No public Markdown implementation is used. - Label matching uses str.casefold plus whitespace collapse. - Unicode punctuation is classified with unicodedata categories P* and S*. - Soft breaks are rendered as a line ending. - The executable must run under plain python3 with no virtual environment activated. ## story executable-interface summary: Provide the executable ./commonmark: UTF-8 stdin to HTML stdout, line intake, and README. type: service kind: capability phase: 1 implements: FEATURE-Executable.md covers: CMK-001 stack: common.md, python.md provides: ./commonmark (stdin Markdown to stdout HTML) consumes: mdparser package depends: foundation acceptance: yes instructions: | Create the executable file commonmark at the application root. It has a python3 shebang, the executable bit set, and puts its own directory on sys.path so it works without any activated environment. Read all of stdin as bytes and decode as UTF-8 with U+FFFD replacement for invalid bytes. Normalize line endings: LF, CR and CRLF are all line endings. Replace U+0000 with U+FFFD. Pass the lines to the parser entry point in mdparser.cli and write only the rendered HTML to stdout as UTF-8. Diagnostics go to stderr only. Exit 0 on all input, with no traceback. Empty input gives empty output and exit 0. Until the block engine story lands, the parser entry point may be a minimal placeholder that renders no blocks. Write a concise README.md describing the stdin/stdout interface. README content is not an acceptance criterion. Surfaced criteria to carry as bounded acceptance checks, using subprocess with input=: - AC-001: empty stdin gives empty stdout and exit status 0. - AC-002: invalid UTF-8 bytes give exit status 0, no traceback on stderr, and no failure. - AC-003: stdout carries only rendered HTML. Check this through the exit status, and by confirming the output contains no diagnostic marker the criterion itself supplied. ## story block-engine summary: Implement the Appendix phase 1 block engine and paragraph rendering with HTML escaping. type: service kind: capability phase: 1 implements: FEATURE-Block-Engine.md covers: CMK-002 stack: common.md, python.md provides: block tree builder, paragraph renderer, HTML escaping and URL percent-encoding helpers consumes: ./commonmark depends: executable-interface acceptance: yes instructions: | Implement the per-line procedure from the Appendix: 1. Match the open blocks, without closing unmatched ones yet because of lazy continuation. 2. Look for new block starts and close the unmatched blocks before creating them. 3. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block. Use a document tree with an extensible block-type registry, so each later block story only adds a start rule, a continue rule and a close rule. Implement document, paragraph and blank-line handling. Paragraph raw content strips initial and final spaces and tabs. Later paragraph lines may have any indentation. The renderer emits p elements, escapes & < > and ", and holds the shared URL percent-encoding helper that link stories reuse. Phase 2 walks the tree and calls an inline parser hook. Until the inline stories land, that hook returns the escaped text. Acceptance for this story is bounded and uses state oracles: - Count p elements for a supplied number of blank-line-separated paragraphs. - Check that exit status is 0. - Check that supplied special characters appear escaped, not raw. The Paragraphs and Blank lines corpus sections need indented code, hard breaks and ATX headings. They are gated in the cont-tabs-slice story and in the terminal story, not here. ## story autolinks summary: Parse URI and email autolinks. type: service kind: capability phase: 2 implements: FEATURE-Autolinks.md covers: INL-007 stack: common.md, python.md provides: autolink inline construct consumes: inline parser hook depends: block-engine acceptance: yes instructions: | Implement URI autolinks (scheme of 2 to 32 characters, then a colon, then no control characters, space, < or >) and email autolinks (the HTML5 regex from the spec, rendered with a mailto: prefix). Backslash escapes are inert inside autolinks. Percent-encode non-ASCII and unsafe characters in the href with the shared helper, and HTML-escape the link text. Gate: python3 sources/spec_tests.py --program ./commonmark --spec sources/spec.txt --pattern '^Autolinks$' with Suite: scoped. The section needs only paragraphs. ## story raw-html-inline summary: Parse raw inline HTML tags, comments, processing instructions, declarations and CDATA. type: service kind: capability phase: 2 implements: FEATURE-Raw-HTML.md covers: INL-008 stack: common.md, python.md provides: raw inline HTML construct consumes: inline parser hook depends: block-engine acceptance: yes instructions: | Implement the open tag, closing tag, comment (including the and forms), processing instruction, declaration and CDATA grammars exactly as given in the spec, including attributes with up to one line ending in whitespace positions. Matching tags are emitted unescaped. Everything else is escaped text. Backslash escapes are inert in raw HTML. Acceptance is bounded: supplied tag strings pass through, and supplied illegal forms are escaped, checked with state oracles. The corpus section Raw HTML has one example that needs block quotes. It is gated in the cont-tabs-slice story. ## story code-spans summary: Parse code spans and establish the inline precedence order. type: service kind: capability phase: 2 implements: FEATURE-Code-Spans.md covers: INL-001 stack: common.md, python.md provides: code span inline construct, inline scanner loop consumes: autolink inline construct, raw inline HTML construct depends: autolinks, raw-html-inline acceptance: yes instructions: | Implement the inline scanner: a left-to-right loop where code spans, autolinks and raw HTML bind equally tightly and the first one found wins. Backtick strings must match by exact length. Convert line endings to spaces, then strip one leading and one trailing space only when the content is not all spaces. Backslash escapes are inert in code spans. Unmatched backtick runs are literal. Gate: --pattern '^Code spans$|^Inlines$' with Suite: scoped. The Precedence section needs lists and is gated in the lists story. ## story backslash-escapes summary: Implement backslash escapes in text, destinations, titles and info strings. type: service kind: capability phase: 2 implements: FEATURE-Backslash-Escapes.md covers: INL-002 stack: common.md, python.md provides: backslash escape inline rule, shared unescape helper consumes: inline scanner loop depends: code-spans acceptance: yes instructions: | Any ASCII punctuation may be escaped. A backslash before any other character is literal. A backslash at the end of a line is a hard break marker, handled by the line-breaks story. Expose a reusable unescape helper for link destinations, titles and info strings. The corpus section Backslash escapes needs fenced code, links and definitions. It is gated in the cont-tabs-slice story. Acceptance is bounded: escape a supplied punctuation character and check that no emphasis, em, or code element is produced for it, and that the backslash is consumed. ## story entities summary: Decode HTML5 named, decimal and hexadecimal character references. type: service kind: capability phase: 2 implements: FEATURE-Entities.md covers: INL-003 stack: common.md, python.md provides: entity decoding rule, shared entity helper consumes: inline scanner loop depends: backslash-escapes acceptance: yes instructions: | Use html.entities.html5 for names (only forms that end in a semicolon), decimal references of 1 to 7 digits and hexadecimal references of 1 to 6 digits. Replace invalid code points and U+0000 with U+FFFD. Unrecognized references stay literal with & escaped. Decoded characters are always plain text and never structure. Expose the helper for link destinations, titles and info strings. Entities are inert in code spans and code blocks. Acceptance is bounded and derived from supplied inputs: for example, a numeric reference built from a bound code point must yield the chr() of that value, HTML-escaped where needed. The corpus section is gated in the cont-tabs-slice story. ## story emphasis summary: Implement the delimiter stack, flanking rules, and the process-emphasis algorithm. type: service kind: capability phase: 2 implements: FEATURE-Emphasis.md covers: INL-004 stack: common.md, python.md provides: delimiter stack, process_emphasis procedure consumes: inline scanner loop depends: entities acceptance: yes instructions: | Follow the Appendix algorithm. Delimiter runs of * and _ are text nodes pushed on the stack with can_open and can_close computed from the flanking rules (Unicode whitespace and punctuation). Implement process emphasis with stack_bottom, openers_bottom indexed by delimiter type, closer length mod 3 and closer-can-open, the multiple-of-3 rule, strong versus regular emphasis selection, and removal of delimiters between the matched pair. The stack must also accept [ and ![ entries, so the links story can reuse it. Expose process_emphasis(stack_bottom). Acceptance is bounded and structural: em and strong element counts for supplied simple inputs. The corpus section Emphasis and strong emphasis needs links and is gated in the images story. ## story link-reference-definitions summary: Extract link reference definitions when a paragraph closes and provide label normalization. type: service kind: capability phase: 2 implements: FEATURE-Link-Reference-Definitions.md covers: LEAF-007 stack: common.md, python.md provides: reference map, normalize_label consumes: block tree builder depends: block-engine acceptance: yes instructions: | On paragraph close, repeatedly parse leading definitions: a label (at most 999 characters, no unescaped brackets, at least one non-whitespace character), a colon, an optional line ending, a destination (angle form or plain, balanced parentheses), an optional title (double, single or parenthesized, may span lines but contains no blank line), and then end of line. The first definition for a normalized label wins. A definition cannot interrupt a paragraph, which follows from extracting only at the start of the paragraph's text. Any remainder stays a paragraph, and an all-definition paragraph disappears. normalize_label strips the brackets, applies str.casefold(), strips, and collapses internal spaces, tabs and line endings to a single space. Definitions in containers still go in the one document-wide map. The inline stories consume the map. Acceptance is bounded: a document that consists only of a definition renders nothing (empty stdout apart from whitespace), and a definition followed by a supplied paragraph renders one p element. The corpus section is gated in the cont-tabs-slice story because its examples need headings, quotes and links. ## story links summary: Implement link and image bracket handling: inline, full, collapsed and shortcut forms. type: service kind: capability phase: 2 implements: FEATURE-Links.md covers: INL-005 stack: common.md, python.md provides: look_for_link_or_image procedure, link destination and title grammar consumes: delimiter stack, process_emphasis procedure, reference map, normalize_label depends: emphasis, link-reference-definitions acceptance: yes instructions: | On ] run look-for-link-or-image per the Appendix: find the nearest [ or ![ opener, handle inactive openers, then try an inline link (destination grammar including the angle form, balanced parentheses, up to one line ending, and a title), a full reference, a collapsed reference, then a shortcut reference through the reference map. Run process_emphasis with the opener as stack_bottom. After a successful link (not image), deactivate earlier [ openers. Handle ![ openers with the same machinery, but leave image rendering to the images story. Destinations and titles go through unescape, entity decoding and URL percent-encoding of non-ASCII and unsafe characters. Backslash-escaped brackets and code spans, autolinks and raw HTML bind more tightly than brackets. Acceptance is bounded: inline links with supplied text and destination (checked as an a element count and returned state), links in links not nested, and an unresolved shortcut reference staying literal. The Links corpus section needs images. It is gated in the images story. ## story images summary: Render images with plain-text alt and verify links, images and emphasis against the corpus. type: service kind: capability phase: 2 implements: FEATURE-Images.md covers: INL-006 stack: common.md, python.md provides: image rendering consumes: look_for_link_or_image procedure depends: links acceptance: yes instructions: | Render img with src, alt and optional title. The alt is the plain-text content of the description, with formatting and nested links reduced to their text content and HTML-escaped. All four link forms apply to images. Gate: --pattern '^Emphasis and strong emphasis$|^Links$|^Images$' with Suite: scoped. All three sections are satisfiable at this point with the inline stories and the reference map. The Link reference definitions section is gated in the cont-tabs-slice story. ## story line-breaks-text summary: Implement hard and soft line breaks and plain textual content. type: service kind: capability phase: 2 implements: FEATURE-Line-Breaks-Text.md covers: INL-009 stack: common.md, python.md provides: hard break and soft break inline nodes consumes: inline scanner loop depends: images acceptance: yes instructions: | A line ending preceded by two or more spaces or a backslash, not at the end of a block, is a hard break rendered as
followed by a line ending. Leading spaces on the next line are dropped. Any other line ending is a soft break rendered as a line ending, with spaces dropped on both sides. Breaks are inert in code spans and raw HTML. Plain text keeps internal spaces verbatim. Gate: --pattern '^Soft line breaks$|^Textual content$' with Suite: scoped. The Hard line breaks section uses ATX headings and is gated in the cont-tabs-slice story. ## story thematic-breaks summary: Parse thematic breaks. type: service kind: capability phase: 3 implements: FEATURE-Thematic-Breaks.md covers: LEAF-001 stack: common.md, python.md provides: thematic break block consumes: block-type registry depends: line-breaks-text acceptance: yes instructions: | Up to three spaces of indentation, then three or more matching -, _ or * characters with optional spaces or tabs between and after them, and no other characters. A thematic break interrupts a paragraph and takes precedence over a list item start. The setext-underline precedence is wired in the setext story. Acceptance is bounded and uses state oracles on hr element counts for supplied marker lines. The corpus section needs lists and setext, so it is gated in the lists story. ## story atx-headings summary: Parse ATX headings. type: service kind: capability phase: 3 implements: FEATURE-ATX-Headings.md covers: LEAF-002 stack: common.md, python.md provides: ATX heading block consumes: block-type registry, inline parser hook depends: thematic-breaks acceptance: yes instructions: | Opening run of 1 to 6 # followed by space, tab or end of line, with up to three spaces of indentation. Drop an optional closing run of unescaped # preceded by whitespace, and strip the content before inline parsing. A heading interrupts a paragraph and can be empty. Gate: --pattern '^ATX headings$' with Suite: scoped. This is satisfiable because indented code is a plain paragraph fallthrough for the single indented example only if the indented-code story has landed. To avoid that coupling, the acceptance is bounded here (heading level counts for supplied levels and the seven-hash case). The corpus section is gated in the lists story. ## story indented-code summary: Parse indented code blocks. type: service kind: capability phase: 3 implements: FEATURE-Indented-Code.md covers: LEAF-004 stack: common.md, python.md provides: indented code block consumes: block-type registry depends: atx-headings acceptance: yes instructions: | Four or more columns of indentation, column-aware with tab stops of 4, on a non-blank line that is not a paragraph continuation. Chunks are separated by blank lines. Interior blank lines keep indentation beyond four columns, and leading and trailing blank lines are dropped. Content is literal and escaped. There is no info string. Acceptance is bounded. The corpus section needs lists and is gated in the lists story. ## story fenced-code summary: Parse fenced code blocks with info strings. type: service kind: capability phase: 3 implements: FEATURE-Fenced-Code.md covers: LEAF-005 stack: common.md, python.md provides: fenced code block consumes: block-type registry, backslash and entity helpers depends: indented-code acceptance: yes instructions: | An opening fence is at least three backticks or tildes with up to three spaces of indentation. Backtick info strings may not contain backticks. A closing fence uses the same character, is at least as long, and has up to three spaces of indentation followed only by spaces or tabs. Remove up to N spaces of indentation from content lines, where N is the opening fence indentation. An unclosed fence runs to the end of the document or container. The first word of the info string, after unescape and entity decoding, becomes class="language-WORD". A fence can interrupt a paragraph. Acceptance is bounded. The corpus section needs code spans, quotes, lists and setext, and is gated in the lists story. ## story html-blocks summary: Parse the seven kinds of HTML block. type: service kind: capability phase: 3 implements: FEATURE-HTML-Blocks.md covers: LEAF-006 stack: common.md, python.md provides: HTML block consumes: block-type registry depends: fenced-code acceptance: yes instructions: | Implement start and end conditions 1 to 7 exactly as given, including the case-insensitive type 6 tag list, the complete-tag requirement for type 7, and the rule that type 7 cannot interrupt a paragraph. Lines are emitted raw. Block types 1 to 5 end on the end-condition line, and types 6 and 7 end before a blank line. Blocks end at the end of the container. Acceptance is bounded. The corpus section needs quotes, lists and indented code, and is gated in the cont-tabs-slice story. ## story block-quotes summary: Parse block quotes with laziness and consecutiveness rules. type: service kind: capability phase: 3 implements: FEATURE-Block-Quotes.md covers: CONT-001 stack: common.md, python.md provides: block quote container consumes: block-type registry, lazy continuation check depends: html-blocks acceptance: yes instructions: | A marker is > with up to three spaces of indentation and an optional following space (a tab counts as columns). Implement the container continue rule, lazy paragraph continuation (only when the line would continue a paragraph), and the blank-line separation rule. Nested quotes can omit the leading > on lazy lines. Acceptance is bounded: blockquote element counts and nesting depth for supplied inputs. The corpus section needs lists and is gated in the lists story. ## story setext-headings summary: Parse setext headings, including multiline content and underline precedence. type: service kind: capability phase: 3 implements: FEATURE-Setext-Headings.md covers: LEAF-003 stack: common.md, python.md provides: setext heading block consumes: paragraph block, thematic break block depends: block-quotes acceptance: yes instructions: | An underline of = (level 1) or - (level 2) with up to three spaces of indentation and trailing whitespace only, which follows a paragraph that is not itself in a lazy-continuation position, turns the whole paragraph (multiple lines) into a heading. It takes precedence over a thematic break. Link definitions that were already extracted from the paragraph's start do not become heading text. Acceptance is bounded. The corpus section is gated in the lists story. ## story list-items summary: Parse list items: markers, indentation rules, empty items, start numbers and laziness. type: service kind: capability phase: 3 implements: FEATURE-List-Items.md covers: CONT-002 stack: common.md, python.md provides: list item container consumes: block-type registry depends: setext-headings acceptance: yes instructions: | Bullet markers are -, + and *. Ordered markers are 1 to 9 digits followed by . or ). Implement the content-offset computation (W + N for 1 to 4 spaces, W + 1 when the content is 5 or more spaces because it starts with an indented code block, and W + 1 for an item starting with a blank line), the column-aware continuation, at-most-one leading blank line, lazy continuation, and the interruption rules: an empty item or a non-1 ordered start cannot interrupt a paragraph, and the thematic break takes precedence. Acceptance is bounded. The List items corpus section needs list grouping and is gated in the lists story. ## story lists summary: Group list items into lists and compute tight or loose rendering. type: service kind: capability phase: 3 implements: FEATURE-Lists.md covers: CONT-003 stack: common.md, python.md provides: list container, tight/loose computation consumes: list item container depends: list-items acceptance: yes instructions: | Group items of the same type: the same bullet character, or the same ordered delimiter. A start number is taken from the first item and emitted as the start attribute only when it is not 1. A list is loose if any two items are separated by a blank line, or if an item directly contains two block children with a blank line between them. Blank lines inside fenced code, inside nested lists' own children, or inside quotes do not count. In a tight list, paragraphs render without p tags. Output the exact structure required by the spec examples. Gate: --pattern '^Lists$|^List items$|^Block quotes$|^Thematic breaks$|^ATX headings$|^Setext headings$|^Indented code blocks$|^Fenced code blocks$|^Precedence$' with Suite: scoped. All block constructs and all inline constructs those sections use have been built by this point. ## story cont-tabs-slice summary: Make tab columns work for block structure and verify the remaining corpus sections. type: service kind: capability phase: 3 implements: FEATURE-Tabs.md covers: CONT-004 stack: common.md, python.md provides: tab-stop-aware column handling consumes: block container rules depends: lists acceptance: yes instructions: | Tabs are never expanded in content. In places where spaces define structure (indented code, block quote and list continuation, and list marker content offsets) a tab advances to the next multiple of 4 columns, and a partially consumed tab leaves its remaining columns as spaces. Audit all the block stories' column handling for this. Gate: --pattern '^Tabs$|^Link reference definitions$|^Backslash escapes$|^Entity and numeric character references$|^Raw HTML$|^HTML blocks$|^Paragraphs$|^Blank lines$|^Hard line breaks$' with Suite: scoped. Together with the other stories' slices this covers every example section. ## story verify-conformance summary: Run the complete supplied CommonMark conformance suite unfiltered. type: feature kind: integration phase: 4 implements: FEATURE-Verification.md accepts: st-001 covers: VER-001 stack: common.md, python.md consumes: ./commonmark depends: foundation, executable-interface, block-engine, autolinks, raw-html-inline, code-spans, backslash-escapes, entities, emphasis, link-reference-definitions, links, images, line-breaks-text, thematic-breaks, atx-headings, indented-code, fenced-code, html-blocks, block-quotes, setext-headings, list-items, lists, cont-tabs-slice acceptance: yes instructions: | Assembly story and the terminal story. Its one Programmatic Acceptance block declares Suite: full, runs sh sources/full_test.sh from the build directory with subprocess (text=True, capture_output=True), prints the captured stdout and stderr, and asserts only result.returncode == 0. Do not invoke full_test.sh from any other story. Do not add file-presence or staged-asset checks. If the suite fails, the repair belongs in the parser, never in the supplied scoring assets. === END ARTIFACT ===

The corpus section Emphasis and strong emphasis needs links and is gated in the images story. ## story link-reference-definitions summary: Extract link reference definitions when a paragraph closes and provide label normalization. type: service kind: capability phase: 2 implements: FEATURE-Link-Reference-Definitions.md covers: LEAF-007 stack: common.md, python.md provides: reference map, normalize_label consumes: block tree builder depends: block-engine acceptance: yes instructions: | On paragraph close, repeatedly parse leading definitions: a label (at most 999 characters, no unescaped brackets, at least one non-whitespace character), a colon, an optional line ending, a destination (angle form or plain, balanced parentheses), an optional title (double, single or parenthesized, may span lines but contains no blank line), and then end of line. The corpus section is gated in the cont-tabs-slice story because its examples need headings, quotes and links. ## story links summary: Implement link and image bracket handling: inline, full, collapsed and shortcut forms. type: service kind: capability phase: 2 implements: FEATURE-Links.md covers: INL-005 stack: common.md, python.md provides: look_for_link_or_image procedure, link destination and title grammar consumes: delimiter stack, process_emphasis procedure, reference map, normalize_label depends: emphasis, link-reference-definitions acceptance: yes instructions: | On ] run look-for-link-or-image per the Appendix: find the nearest [ or ![ opener, handle inactive openers, then try an inline link (destination grammar including the angle form, balanced parentheses, up to one line ending, and a title), a full reference, a collapsed reference, then a shortcut reference through the reference map.
